newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan may change rules for winning ODA projects.
newsitem.headline: Japan may change rules for winning ODA projects.

text.p: Japan plans to review the bidding rules for its lucrative foreign aid projects, a move which could help more Japanese firms win contracts over foreign rivals, a Japanese newspaper reported on Sunday.
The Asahi Shimbun said the government would announce new rules this spring for assessing bids for yen-loan development projects.
The newspaper said the change by the government's Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund (OCEF) could provoke an outcry from European and American firms.
It said the main change was a stricter emphasis on technological evaluation in deciding bids.
The Asahi quoted an OECF official as saying the rule change was intended to improve the quality of the projects, not to favour Japanese firms.
"We must improve the quality of yen-loan projects as much as possible," the official said.
Japanese companies won only 17 percent of yen-loan project contracts in 1995, compared to 62 percent in 1989, the paper reported.
Companies based in developing countries won 60 percent and European and American firms won 13 percent of bids in 1995.
OECF officials were not available to comment on the report. ($1 = 121.3 yen)
